title.value: A Conceptual Framework for Representing Events Under Public Health Surveillance
title.justification: The title specifically refers to a conceptual framework for representing events within the domain of public health surveillance.
title.quote: A Conceptual Framework for Representing Events Under Public Health Surveillance

extractions.description: The paper proposes a conceptual framework to improve integration across multiple event-based surveillance (EBS) systems in public health. It addresses the lack of a common framework for encoding data, which is essential for semantic interoperability and improved disease outbreak detection. The framework aims to represent events and related concepts clearly to facilitate better alignment among EBS systems.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper primarily focuses on improving public health surveillance systems and their semantic interoperability. While this is indirectly related to sustainable development, it does not directly address Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: In practice, however, integration does not occur due to the lack of a common conceptual framework for encoding data within EBS systems.

primary_category.justification: The central theme of this paper is public health surveillance rather than any aspect of Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development.
primary_category.quote: Event-based surveillance (EBS) is the process of monitoring for, and reporting on, events of potential public health importance using information sources not specifically designed for this purpose.

secondary_categories.justification: As the primary focus is not on Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development, there aren't any relevant secondary categories to be identified.
secondary_categories.quote: A common approach is to view an event as a stage in the alerting process, for example: “Once the signal has been triaged and verified, it becomes an event”.

primary_sub_category.justification: Given that the paper does not primarily address any sub-category related to Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development, it is classified as N/A.
primary_sub_category.quote: In this initial modelling stage, we do not assume a specific formal encoding of our framework.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: No secondary sub-categories are relevant as the paper's focus is outside the scope of Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: Following [13], we believe that it is important to represent documents (e.g. media re- ports) about public health events, their sub-events, and associated events explicitly.

applications.justification: The paper discusses the integration of EBS systems to improve global disease surveillance by using a common conceptual framework, which is an application within public health domains.
applications.quote: We aim to address this gap by proposing a candidate conceptual framework for representing events and related concepts in the domain of public health surveillance.

new_primary_category.justification: The existing categories do not fit as the focus is on public health rather than Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development.
new_primary_category.quote: Reaching consensus regarding these high-level concepts should create a foundation for achieving semantic interoperability amongst systems, improving global EBS.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: There is no need for a new category as the focus remains outside the established Climate/Ecological Sustainable Development scope.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: Most frameworks agree that events have temporal boundaries, i.e. a distinct start and end time points.
